If I get rejected from y, I'll move to my second choice, x. I have priority rank 2 at x. Since most applicants seem to prefer y > x > w > z, there's a good chance I might be accepted at x if I'm rejected from y.

If I get rejected from x, I'll move to my third choice, z. I have priority rank 2 at z.

If I get rejected from z, I'll move to my last choice, w. I have priority rank 1 at w.

This strategy aligns with the DA algorithm and maximizes my chances of getting a good match.
